title: Fabricating Superhydrophobic Polymeric Materials for Biomedical Applications
protocol: Dissolve cis-2-Phenyl-1,3-dioxan-5-ol (50 g) in 500 ml dry tetrahydrofuran (THF) and stir on ice under nitrogen.
Add potassium hydroxide (33.5 g), finely crushed with a mortar and pestle.
Place the flask in an ice bath.
Add benzyl bromide (49.6 ml) drop-wise to the mixture while stirring on ice.
Allow the reaction to warm to room temperature and stir for 24 hr under nitrogen.
Add 150 ml distilled water to dissolve potassium hydroxide and remove THF by rotary evaporation.
Extract remaining material with dichloromethane (DCM).
Dry the organic phase on sodium sulfate.
Crystallize the product by adding absolute ethanol to the solution, mixing well, and storing overnight at -20 °C.
Isolate the product by vacuum-filtration through a Büchner funnel and dry on high-vacuum.
Suspend the product obtained in step 1.1.7. in methanol (300 ml).
Add 150 ml of 2 N hydrochloric acid to the suspension.
Reflux at 80 °C for 2 hr.
Evaporate solvent.
Place under high-vacuum for 24 hours.
Dissolve product in THF (650 ml).
Transfer solution to a 2-L round-bottom flask.
Place flask on an ice bath and stir under nitrogen.
Add ethyl chloroformate (22.4 ml) to the flask under nitrogen.
Mix triethylamine (32.8 ml) with an equal volume of THF.
Carefully dispense the triethylamine/THF mixture drop-wise into the round-bottom flask on ice, no faster than 1 drop per second.
Stir the reaction for 4 hours at room temperature or for 24 hours.
Filter out the triethylamine hydrochloride salt using a Büchner funnel.
Evaporate the solvent on a rotary evaporator.
Add dichloromethane (200 ml) to the flask and heat gently until the residue is dissolved.
Add diethyl ether (120 ml) while swirling.
Store at -20 °C overnight to crystallize the product.
Filter monomer crystals.
Re-crystallize before polymerizing.
Confirm product by 1H NMR, mass spectrometry, and elemental analysis.
Heat silicone oil bath to 140 °C.
Measure 2.1 g of 5-benzyloxy-1,3-dioxan-2-one and add it to a dry 100-ml round-bottom flask.
If copolymerizing D,L-lactide, measure out 5.7 g and add to the flask now.
Add a magnetic stir bar and seal the flask with a rubber stopper.
Measure 240 mg of tin(II) ethylhexanoate in a small pear-shaped flask.
Flush both flasks with nitrogen on a Schlenk manifold for 5 min.
Add 4.24 ml ε-caprolactone under nitrogen to each flask.
Evacuate the flasks’ atmosphere by applying high-vacuum (300 mTorr) for 15 min to remove trace water.
Recharge the flasks’ atmosphere with nitrogen; repeat this cycle twice more.
Mix 500 µl dry toluene with the tin catalyst under nitrogen.
Place the monomer flask in the 140 °C oil bath and add catalyst once all solids have melted.
Keep at 140 °C for no more than 24 hr, then cool the molten polymer to room temperature.
Dissolve the polymer in dichloromethane (50 ml).
Precipitate the dissolved polymer into cold methanol (200 ml).
Decant the supernatant.
Dry under high-vacuum.
Perform 1H NMR analysis to determine the co-monomer molar ratios.
Dissolve polymer in deuterated chloroform (CDCl3).
Integrate the benzylic proton shift of the carbonate monomer at 4.58-4.68 ppm.
Compare this peak area with that of the methylene peak at 2.3 ppm (PCL) and methyne peak at 5.2 ppm (PLGA).
Dissolve polymer (~7 g) in 120 ml tetrahydrofuran (THF) in a high-pressure hydrogenation vessel.
Weigh and add palladium-carbon catalyst (~2 g).
Add hydrogen to the vessel using a hydrogenation apparatus.
Hydrogenate at 50 psi for 4 hr.
Filter out palladium-carbon catalyst using a packed bed of diatomaceous earth.
Concentrate the polymer to ~50 ml under rotary evaporation.
Precipitate the concentrated solution into cold methanol.
Dry the precipitated material under high-vacuum.
Confirm total conversion to free hydroxyl by noting peak disappearance at 4.65 ppm in CDCl3 NMR.
Dissolve the polymer and stearic acid (1.5 eq.) in 500 ml dry dichloromethane (DCM).
Add N,N’-dicyclohexylcarbodiimide (DCC, 2.0 eq.) and 3 flakes of 4-dimethylaminopyridine.
Stir under nitrogen at room temperature for 24 hr.
Remove insoluble N,N’-dicyclohexylcarbourea through a series of repeated filtrations.
Concentrate the solution to 50 ml.
Precipitate polymer into cold methanol (~175 ml).
Decant the supernatant from the precipitated polymer.
Dry the polymer under high-vacuum overnight.
Weigh out ~10 mg of polymer and record the actual mass.
Add weighed polymer to an aluminum sample pan.
Hermetically seal the sample pan containing the polymer.
Load the sealed sample pan into a differential scanning calorimeter.
Load an unloaded (reference) pan into the differential scanning calorimeter alongside the sample pan.
Program a temperature ramp from 20 °C to 225 °C at 10 °C/min in the DSC.
Cool the sample to -75 °C at 5 °C/min.
Heat the sample back to 225 °C at 10 °C/min.
Determine melting point (Tm) from the thermal traces.
Determine crystallization temperature (Tc) from the thermal traces.
Determine glass transition temperature (Tg) from the thermal traces.
Determine heat of fusion (ΔHf) from the thermal traces.
Dissolve each synthesized copolymer in THF at 1 mg/ml concentration.
Filter the solution through a 0.02-µm PTFE filter.
Inject the filtered solution into a gel permeation chromatography system.
Compare retention time versus a range of polystyrene standards.
Dissolve polymer(s) at 10-40 wt% in suitable solvent for electrospinning/electrospraying.
Choose chloroform/methanol (5:1) as the solvent for PCL.
Choose tetrahydrofuran/N,N-dimethylformamide (7:3) as the solvent for PLGA.
Dissolve polymer(s) overnight in the chosen solvent.
Vortex polymer solution to thoroughly mix.
Allow large air bubbles to subside for 5 minutes.
Load solution into a glass syringe.
Invert the syringe to displace air through the hose/needle assembly.
Cover the collector plate with aluminum foil.
Secure the foil with masking tape along the outer edges.
Attach the high voltage DC supply wire to the needle tip.
Set the distance between the needle tip and the collector plate to 15 cm.
Load the syringe onto the syringe pump.
Set the total volume (e.g., 4.5 ml) on the syringe pump.
Set the rate at which to dispense the solution (e.g., 5 ml/hr).
Provide adequate ventilation for outside exhaust.
Do not touch the syringe/needle or open the enclosure until certain the HVDC supply is off.
Start the syringe pump.
Adjust the high voltage source to achieve an acceptable Taylor Cone.
Increase the voltage if the solution at the needle tip is sagging.
Reduce the voltage if multiple jets are forming.
Adjust the tip-to-collector distance if fibers/particles appear wet or adjusting the voltage does not solve a dragging droplet.
Turn off the high voltage source after completing the process.
Turn off the syringe pump after turning off the high voltage source.
Turn off the motorized drum (if applicable) and allow the electrospinning enclosure to ventilate for 30 minutes.
Remove meshes/coatings from collector once ventilation is complete.
Allow trace solvents to evaporate in a hood overnight.
Cut and mount thin portions of an electrospun mesh on a glass slide for light microscopy observation.
Observe fiber diameter, node characteristics (blobs or discrete), and fiber shape (beaded, flat, straight/wavy) under the microscope.
Prepare samples for scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis.
Cut meshes or coated surfaces into strips and mount them on aluminum SEM stubs using conductive copper tape.
Coat the mounted samples with a thin (~4 nm) layer of Au/Pd through sputter coating.
Load the coated stubs into the SEM chamber and observe at 1-2 keV.
Use 250X magnification to assess general topographical features of the material.
Increase magnifications to reveal additional fiber and particle features such as hierarchical patterns for superhydrophobic fibers and interconnectivity for particle coatings.
Cut thin (0.5 cm x 5 cm) strips of mesh or coated material and place them on a contact angle goniometer stage.
Dispense an approximate 5-µl drop from a 24 AWG syringe needle onto the material surface.
Continue to slowly add volume (20-25 µl) while capturing droplet images to determine advancing water contact angles.
Prepare an 80 mg/ml solution of Ioxaglate in water.
Submerge meshes in the solutions.
Incubate at 37 °C.
Measure contrast agent infiltration by µCT with a voxel resolution of 18 µm³.
Use a tube voltage of 70 kVP and current of 114 µA, with an integration time of 300 msec for imaging.
Analyze pixel intensity throughout the thickness of the mesh using image processing software.
Select a pixel threshold value (~1500) to represent water infiltration.
Cut meshes to 1 cm x 7 cm.
Place cut meshes between the grips of a tensile testing apparatus.
Measure the exact width, length, and thickness of the meshes.
Perform a ramp test of extension on three samples.
Plot a stress-strain curve using the data from the tests.
Determine the elastic modulus, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation-at-break from the plotted curve.
